The recurring onboarding blockers are:

1. **Permission mapping / RBAC sync** – the most common blocker, accounting for 45% of delay incidents in implementation logs [NL-031#NL-031-S04] and 45% of delays in Q2 onboarding data [NL-012#NL-012-S06]. The playbook also identifies permission mapping as the most common blocker and dedicates Phase 4 to directory sync and access control [NL-005#NL-005-S06].

2. **Source ingestion cleanup** – removing outdated, redundant, or corrupted documents before indexing, accounting for 30% of delay incidents [NL-031#NL-031-S04] and 30% of Q2 delays [NL-012#NL-012-S06]. The playbook includes stale-document archiving and corpus formatting as part of Phase 3 [NL-005#NL-005-S02].

3. **OCR / scanned PDF processing** – extracting readable text from image-only legacy PDFs, accounting for 25% of delay incidents [NL-031#NL-031-S04] and 25% of Q2 delays [NL-012#NL-012-S06]. The playbook lists OCR processing of scanned legacy documents as an enterprise complexity [NL-005#NL-005-S02] and provides an advanced OCR queue for heritage PDFs [NL-005#NL-005-S09].

No separate customer-interview evidence was supplied in the context; the recurrence is established from the playbook, implementation logs, and Q2 implementation data. Enterprise-specific items such as security/SSO/retention reviews also delayed individual customers, e.g., Northstar Financial [NL-012#NL-012-S06], but the recurring blocker categories named consistently are the three above.
